newsitem.title: UK: Blair says new business generation trusts Labour.
newsitem.headline: Blair says new business generation trusts Labour.

text.p: Labour leader Tony Blair is set to proclaim on Tuesday that Britain's new generation of corporate leaders is increasingly identifying with his party, changing the traditional link between business and the Conservatives.

Keeping up the pressure on the Conservatives after Monday's pledge by Labour's economics spokesman Gordon Brown to peg taxes and spending, Blair is using a report by business leaders to highlight Labour's improving links with business.

The report, issued by the left-leaning Institute for Public Policy Research but compiled by businessmen including British Aerospace Chairman Bob Bauman and J Sainsbury chairman David Sainsbury, is expected to criticise Britain's competitiveness.

The report is also expected to demand radical policies from whichever party wins the looming election to tackle the problems of too little investment, too many school-leavers underachieving and too many shifts in government policy.
Senior Labour aides said Blair is delighted that the report chimes so closely with Labour's stated policies for business.

And Blair is expected to use his speech to say that this shows Labour's efforts to improve dialogue with the business community has moved beyond reassurance to the stage where it is now the sound basis for partnership.

Blair is also expected to say that New Labour, as he has dubbed the party he has dragged from the left to the centre, represents a new generation in politics in the same way a new generation is taking over the British business establishment.
He is also expected to announce the creation of a three-man strong body to study the report's recommendations.

Blair, who is due to unveil new proposals for welfare reform later in the week in a speech in the Netherlands, is also expected to use his speech to give more details of Labour's plans to overhaul competition policy if it takes power.
